candidates.title: Leaf (uarch-level) commitment budget is sized to average uarch density: a dense run of heavy instructions in one level-0 stride makes the honest inner-claim build take 2-7x the 120-minute budget, so the honest claim misses the inner tournament's closure (testnet) or drains the censorship budget per forced delegation (mainnet)
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 released constants and clock model (ArbitrationConstants, ClockBudgets, Deployment.s.sol), together with collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes (the uarch-level claim builder)
candidates.role: Referee model (deployed referee: dispute constants and clocks); the operation whose cost overruns, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, is Honest operator
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ArbitrationConstants.sol (COMMITMENT_BUDGET = 120 minutes; log2step [38,0], height [54,38]); ClockBudgets.sol refill()/maxAllowance(); Tournament.sol joinTournament (initializePausedAt deducts lateness; _isClosed at startInstant+allowance), sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament (child allowance = max(r1,r2)); prt/contracts/script/Deployment.s.sol _registerChainKinds (C = 1 week MAINNET, 8 h TESTNET, 0 DEVNET), _getInclusionBudget (5 min); design rationale in bugs/harness/work/dave/released/docs/dimensioning.md 'The rule' ('Clocks are dimensioned to the average case') and docs/measurements/constants.md (table derived at 566 usteps per mcycle); src/machine.cpp collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes.
candidates.description: With the released table, one level-0 leaf spans 2^38 meta-cycles = 2^18 mcycles, and the level-1 (leaf) tournament commits to one hash per uarch cycle over that span. To join the child tournament the honest operator must build that commitment, which costs one uarch step plus a root-hash update per executed uarch cycle (R12: linear in the uarch cycles executed). The deployment grants T = COMMITMENT_BUDGET = 120 min for it (plus G = 5 min inclusion), as a refill on return and as one refill in the root allowance. The table was derived for an AVERAGE density of 566 executed usteps per mcycle (docs/measurements/constants.md: 'clocks price the trusted app's AVERAGE density'); the uarch span per mcycle is 2^20 and real instructions reach 17,586 usteps. Any guest code that is dense in heavy instructions for ~2^18 mcycles (a few milliseconds of guest time: an fdiv/fsqrt-heavy numeric loop in user mode, or sfence.vma in a guest whose kernel an input controlled) makes the honest build exceed T several times over. The overrun is charged to the honest claim as join lateness with no discount (initializePausedAt), and the child tournament closes at startInstant + max(r1, r2), so a build longer than the envelope means the honest inner claim can never join. The adversary chooses the divergence position ('Steer the dispute to any position of the honest computation'), so it steers each match to a dense period.
candidates.trigger: Dishonest claimant posts a root claim that first diverges from the honest claim inside a 2^18-mcycle period where the (correctly designed, or input-controlled) guest runs dense heavy instructions; the match seals there and creates a leaf child tournament. The dishonest side joins its own (cheap to compute: any claim ending at its contested state) inner claim immediately. With Sybils (one root bond each) it repeats this for further dense periods.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template whose guest runs, in some 2^18-mcycle window, floating-point divide/sqrt in a loop (user mode, no privileges needed) or any other heavy instruction stream; THREAT_MODEL section 2 presumes any assignment of guest-writable memory and registers reachable and section 4 lets an input run any instruction stream at any privilege level. No dispute constant bounds usteps per mcycle below 2^20.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The exclusion 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8' does not apply: it carves out 'unless the emulator's own behavior is what makes the obligation fail, such as a worst-case cost ... larger than the deployment was sized for, or unless an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)', and Dave is the deployed referee model (AUDIT.md table). It does not need an application that is not correctly designed: section 2 bounds only the application's mcycle usage ('It bounds its own mcycle usage'), not uarch cycles per mcycle, and R4 says the costs of R12 apply 'for every guest'. 2. Role: Dave contracts = Referee model (AUDIT.md: 'Referee model, as the deployed referee. Audit the released constants'); the uarch-level claim builder collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes = Honest operator. Section 3 caveat: 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond ... is rated as support' could be read to cover clock sizing (then Medium, as a support defect that would be Critical in its stood-in role). 3. High/Medium cases: not a demonstrably unreachable state; not a constant-factor multiplication caused by a defect (the cost is what the specified semantics require). 4. Critical: matches the listed Critical case 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make unbounded, super-linear, or larger than what the deployment was sized for' (a uarch-level claim is listed in R12; the deployment was sized for 120 min at 566 usteps/mcycle; measured 4.3 h (fdiv) to 13.4 h (sfence.vma)). It violates A7: 'The dispute constants and clocks leave room for the honest claim to play the logarithmic number of matches that a tournament forces on it, at the worst-case costs of R12' and 'No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock' (the child closure at startInstant+envelope ends the honest claim's ability to join while it is still building at full speed), and section 1's Completeness failure ('cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win'). 5. n/a.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (alternative reading: Medium, if section 3's 'only changes how long a claim may take to respond' is applied to the referee model's clock sizing)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure. Testnet constants (Sepolia, 12 s blocks): maxAllowance = C + 2G + (T + 2G) = 2400 + 50 + 650 = 3100 blocks = 10.3 h, so every child envelope is at most 10.3 h; a sfence.vma-dense period needs 13.4 h to build on this host (8.4 h even at Dave's own measured 10 us per ustep), so the honest inner claim misses the child's closure, the dishonest inner claim wins the child, winInnerTournament credits the dishonest root claim and deletes the honest root claim's match: the dishonest final state settles. Mainnet (C = 1 week): each forced delegation to a dense period drains build - T (about 2.3 h for fdiv, 11.4 h for sfence.vma on this host) from the non-rechargeable C; about 15 Sybil-forced delegations (one bond each, distinct dense periods) exhaust C and the next one loses the join. Devnet (C = 0): a single overrun of the one-refill reserve loses.
candidates.evidence: Built bare-metal guests (scratch /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/A7/g/*.S: 2-instruction loops of fsqrt.d, fdiv.d, sfence.vma, illegal-instruction trap, fmadd.d) and timed machine:collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes on the in-tree emulator (script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/A7/density.lua and density20.lua, bundle 2^20 as the PRT player uses). Machine load average 0.1-0.5 during the runs. Results (usteps per mcycle avg/max; seconds per mcycle; extrapolated to 2^18 mcycles): fdiv 3060/4620, 0.0586 s, 4.3 h; fsqrt 2486/3777, 0.046 s, 3.4 h; sfence.vma 11200/17586, 0.184 s, 13.4 h; trap 581/619, 1.4 h; fmadd 1075/1518, 1.8 h. Cost is ~17-19 us per uarch cycle (step + hash-tree update), matching Dave's own 173 mcycles/s at 566 usteps (about 10 us/ustep on its reference host). Budget T = 120 min (and the table itself was derived at 60 min). The released docs state the choice explicitly (docs/dimensioning.md: 'Coordinates are dimensioned to the worst case. Clocks are dimensioned to the average case', 'leaf-level dense build within the commitment budget | aggregate | trusted app | average density').
candidates.test_idea: Deterministic, no wall clock: a Lua test builds the fdiv (or sfence.vma) guest, runs collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes over 64 mcycles of the loop, counts executed uarch cycles U (sum over mcycles of hashes before each reset, from mcycle_hash_offsets), and reads the deployed constants from work/dave/released (COMMITMENT_BUDGET, log2step(0)=38, the inclusion budget). It asserts that U * 2^(38-20) / 64 (uarch cycles a 2^18-mcycle dense period executes) times a fixed, documented reference per-uarch-cycle cost (e.g. Dave's own 1/(173*566) s) fits in COMMITMENT_BUDGET; it fails today (fdiv: 3060*2^18/(173*566) s = 2.27 h > 2 h; sfence: 8.3 h). A chain-level variant on the local anvil with released constants and mined blocks: seal a root match at a dense period, mine blocks at the build-time rate, and assert the honest child join is still accepted (it reverts with TournamentIsClosed on testnet constants).

candidates.title: Root allowance has no term for executing the epoch: an adversary floods up to 2^24 inputs and itself calls acceptStagedTournamentResult in the same block, so the honest root join lands its whole execution time late (charged with no discount) or after the root closes
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7: DaveConsensus (sealing at acceptStagedTournamentResult with up to MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH = 2^24 pending inputs) + Tournament.joinTournament / ClockBudgets.maxAllowance
candidates.role: Referee model (deployed referee); the per-input cost is the honest operator's input delivery and run
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol acceptStagedTournamentResult (permissionless; seals [_inputIndexUpperBound, _nextInputIndexUpperBound) at the call's block and instantiates the root at that block), _nextInputIndexUpperBound, MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH = 1 << ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH (24); prt/contracts/src/tournament/Tournament.sol joinTournament (_isClosed; Clock.initializePausedAt: allowance - (now - startInstant)); prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ClockBudgets.sol maxAllowance = C + 2G + (L-1)(T+2G). Acknowledged in bugs/harness/work/dave/released/docs/dimensioning.md 'Aggregate throughput, the second per-app contract'.
candidates.description: The root tournament starts at the block that seals the epoch, and the epoch takes every pending input up to 2^24 at that block. Anyone can call acceptStagedTournamentResult once the staging period is over, so the adversary decides the seal block and can put a burst of inputs in the same block, before its accept call. The honest operator cannot compute its level-0 commitment (the last leaf is the final state) before running all of them. Its root clock is initialized to maxAllowance minus the join's lateness, with no discount, and joins close at startInstant + maxAllowance. The allowance (C + 2G + T + 2G) contains no term for executing the epoch's inputs; the whole execution time is drawn from C, the censorship budget, or makes the join impossible. The honest operator's per-input cost is not zero for any application: delivery, the app's cheapest dismissal, and hashing.
candidates.trigger: Input sender (anyone) adds N inputs to the InputBox for the application in the blocks just before, or in the same block as, its own acceptStagedTournamentResult call, then posts a dishonest root claim early.
candidates.reachability: Any deployment; N up to 2^24 per epoch, and the excess spills into later epochs, each of which can be sealed by the adversary right after a new burst. The threat model grants 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts' and 'Race and reorder transactions within the chain's rules'.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Possibly argued under 'An application that is not correctly designed' if a correctly designed application must keep 'the total within what the deployment was sized for (A7)' even for adversarial input counts; but the per-input overhead (delivery, revert/accept bookkeeping, hashing) is the honest operator's, not the application's mcycle usage, and the input count is chosen by the adversary. Dave's docs make it an extra 'second per-app contract' that THREAT_MODEL does not list. The deployment carve-out does not apply because Dave is the referee model. 2. Role: Referee model (Dave constants and sealing rule); same section 3 caveat as above ('only changes how long a claim may take to respond' -> support, Medium). 3. High/Medium cases: none applies (reachable; not a constant-factor defect). 4. Critical: A7 'The dispute constants and clocks leave room for the honest claim ... while the honest operator also processes the inputs of later epochs' and R4 'The honest operator defends every epoch whose dispute is open ... It assigns inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3)'; the root allowance has no room for the epoch's own execution, so the honest claim loses the join (closure) or its reserve while acting as fast as it can. 5. n/a.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical on deployments with small C (testnet: C = 8 h), High/drain on mainnet with the emulator alone; disputed (Out of scope if the aggregate-throughput app contract is accepted as part of 'correctly designed'; Medium under the section 3 support caveat)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure: the honest claim joins too late to keep the reserve and the refill a forced delegation needs, or misses root closure, so a Sybil's claim wins the root and its final state settles. Measured emulator-only honest cost per input: 6.4 ms (bare-metal accept/emit template) to 9.3 ms (Linux guest-tools echo template, rejected input, 1.27M mcycles): 2^24 inputs = 1.3-1.8 days of execution (drains about a quarter of the mainnet week of C before any dispute), and about 3.1 M inputs already exceed the testnet's entire 8 h C. With the node overhead Dave itself measured (0.14-0.2 s per input) even mainnet loses with about 4.3 M inputs.
candidates.evidence: Read the sealing and join code above; timed send_cmio_response + run + get_root_hash per input with the in-tree emulator on the harness templates (script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/A7/perinput.lua): valid-template 0.0093 s/input, baremetal-template 0.0064 s/input. The released docs/dimensioning.md states 'The root allowance ... holds no term for building the level-0 commitment ... so the honest root join assumes the node has kept up with the epoch's inputs when the epoch seals' and 'Sealing gives no minimum notice either way'.
candidates.test_idea: Chain test with released constants on the local anvil (TESTNET-like C via CanonicalTournamentParametersProvider constructor args): mine to the end of a staging period, add K inputs and call acceptStagedTournamentResult from the adversary in the same block, then advance the chain by K * t_input blocks-equivalent (t_input measured deterministically as mcycles per input times a fixed reference rate) before the honest join. Assert the honest join succeeds with at least maxAllowance - G remaining (the A7 requirement that executing the epoch's own inputs is covered); it fails (TournamentIsClosed, or remaining below the refill) for K above (C+G)/t_input.

candidates.title: PRT stored player runs later-epoch inputs (and agreed-pair replays) in idle steps of one WHOLE input each, non-preemptively, so a response due in the sealed epoch's dispute waits up to a full input run (up to 2^48 mcycles) before the bridge even observes the event
candidates.component: PRT player and crisium main loop (doc/recipes/prt.lua, doc/recipes/crisium.lua)
candidates.role: Support (stands in for the Honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua main loop (pass() only when the tip changed, otherwise idle() one step) and idle(); doc/recipes/prt.lua stored_event_handler.input_added (defers to idle), event_handler.idle -> run_next_input -> run_to_input_mcycle_offset(..., MAX_MCYCLES_PER_ADVANCE_STATE) (runs the input to its fixed point in one call), stored_event_handler.idle / advance_agreed_pair (run_to_epoch_input_offset one whole input per step).
candidates.description: While epoch e is in dispute, the listener of epoch e+1 records its inputs and the honest stored player runs them in idle time. Each idle step runs one entire input to its fixed point (run_to_input_mcycle_offset with input_mcycle_offset = 2^48), and the main loop checks the tip only between steps. A MatchCreated/MatchAdvanced/LeafMatchSealed for the honest claim that lands while an e+1 input runs is not observed until that input finishes; then the response itself may need to replay the disputed input (another full input's cost). The same holds for advance_agreed_pair, which replays one whole input per idle step. The response latency therefore includes one extra worst-case input run, which neither the deployment's per-input sizing nor G accounts for. The comment 'so an open epoch never delays a response in a sealed epoch's dispute' does not hold at input granularity.
candidates.trigger: Input sender adds to epoch e+1 an input on which the (correctly designed) application legitimately computes for a long time (bounded only by imcyclemax), timed just before the dishonest claimant's move that puts the honest claim on turn in epoch e.
candidates.reachability: Every deployment of the player with a non-trivial application; the threat model requires the honest operator to defend 'every epoch whose dispute is open, including while it processes the inputs of later epochs' (R4).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The player is not a test harness or dishonest strategy; in scope (triage applies the 'Support' rating). The trigger is an input the application handles within its own bound, not an application outside its design. 2. Role: AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. 3. High/Medium: falls under the support-Medium case. 4. In the honest-operator role it would violate R4 ('The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks', 'defends every epoch whose dispute is open, including while it processes the inputs of later epochs') and A7, which is Critical; capped to Medium by the support role. 5. n/a.
candidates.threat_to_goal: An honest player with spare clock misses its response window (charged to C, or a timeout loss when C is spent or zero as on devnets), so a dishonest claim can win by timeout; the extra latency equals the longest later-epoch input, which an adversary can schedule.
candidates.evidence: Code reading: crisium.lua 'elseif not idle()' runs idle only when the tip is unchanged, with no tip check inside a step; prt.lua run_next_input calls run_to_input_mcycle_offset with MAX_MCYCLES_PER_ADVANCE_STATE (1 << ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_MCYCLES_PER_ADVANCE_STATE), which runs run_to_stop to the fixed point. The demo harness hides it: it mines the next block only after every player reports the current tip without publishing (prt-lua-bridge.md, 'The demo harness').
candidates.test_idea: Lua test with prt.new_stored_player on a template whose guest spins 2^32 mcycles before yielding (bare-metal builder): seal epoch e of one player, open the e+1 player, add the spinning input as pending, and call event_handler.idle(player) once. Assert that one idle step executes at most a bounded mcycle slice (e.g. checks the machine's mcycle advance per call, or that idle returns before the input reaches its fixed point); today a single call runs the whole input.

candidates.title: PRT bridge keeps a pending cleanup or bond-recovery transaction's nonce while a deadline-bearing response of the honest claim is due, so the response waits for the cleanup's inclusion (including fee-bump rounds)
candidates.component: PRT bridge (doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:tick) and crisium pass ordering
candidates.role: Support (stands in for the Honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:tick: 'for _, job in ipairs(eligible) do if job.key == candidate.job then selected = job' (a still-eligible pending job is preferred over the earliest-expiry job), and 'Another epoch's pending transaction is left alone until it is mined'; one pending transaction per account (prt-transactions.lua).
candidates.description: Jobs are sorted by expiry, but when a transaction is pending and its job is still eligible, the bridge keeps it instead of switching to an earlier-expiring job. Elimination of other claims' matches, child elimination and bond recovery have no expiry and are installed by the honest (cleanup) bridge with the same account. If one of them is pending when a response for the honest claim becomes due, the response is not published until the cleanup transaction is mined; under a base-fee rise its cap (2x base fee + tip at signing) can leave it unmined for several bump rounds (PRT_FEE_BUMP_BLOCKS = 3, +15% each), while a freshly signed response would be included at once. A pending transaction of an older epoch blocks the live epoch the same way.
candidates.trigger: Adversary makes a pair of its own Sybil claims eliminable at block X (or lets a child become eliminable), so the honest bridge publishes the elimination, and puts the honest claim on turn at the same block; optionally raises the base fee by filling blocks.
candidates.reachability: Every deployment of the bridge with cleanup enabled (the honest player in the demo).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Not excluded (bridge, not a harness). 2. Role: Support (AUDIT.md: the PRT player and bridge). 3. Section 3: support defect, Medium only if it would be High/Critical in the honest-operator role; the delay is normally one block, and longer only under fee pressure, so Low is plausible. 4. In the honest-operator role: R4 'submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' and A8 'Failing to process one match's data ... must not stop, delay or decide any other match' (another match's cleanup delays the honest match's response). 5. Low if the delay is considered bounded by inclusion.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Medium if the fee-pressure delay is accepted as reachable)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Spends response budget and C on unrelated cleanup; with C exhausted or zero, a response can miss its deadline.
candidates.evidence: Code reading of methods:tick and the transactions policy described in prt-lua-bridge.md ('Transactions').
candidates.test_idea: prt-bridge-test style fixture: a fake chain with a pending elimination candidate (no expiry) and a newly due respond job whose expiry is tip+2; assert the tick replaces or outbids the pending nonce with the respond job (or at least publishes it), instead of returning with the elimination kept.
